**Repo:** `zealchaiwut/perf-coach`

## Goal
Build the Training Log page — the detailed historical record of every workout. This ticket covers the page shell, the week strip nav, the filter bar, and the grouped list of workouts. The detail side panel ships in a separate ticket.

## Reference mockup
See `/mnt/user-data/outputs/perf-coach-training-log.html`.

## Scope

**New route:** `/log` (or `/training-log` — pick one and document in repo README)

**Page header**
- Title "Training log"
- Subtitle showing last sync time
- Two header buttons: `Export` (CSV download) and `Log workout` (opens manual entry flow — reuse existing if present, stub if not)

**Week strip**
- Horizontal row of 7 day pills (Mon–Sun) for the currently selected week
- Each pill: day-of-week label, day-of-month number, colored dots beneath for workout types (run / lift / wod / bike)
- Today is visually highlighted (soft glow, see mockup)
- Left/right chevron buttons to navigate weeks
- Center label shows "This week" or "May 19 – 25" depending on selection
- Clicking a day pill scrolls the list to that day's row

**Filter bar**
- Search input (placeholder "Search workouts") — filters by title and notes
- Type chips: All / Run / Lift / WOD / Bike (single-select for v1, multi-select can be a follow-up)
- Date range chip (default 30d; opens a date picker for custom)
- Filter state persists in URL query params so a filtered view is shareable and reloadable

**Workout list grouped by week**
- Each week boundary shows a summary row: week label, date range, total workouts, total distance (km), total TSS, total time
- Below the summary, each workout is a single row with this shape:
  - Date column (day-of-month large, day-of-week small)
  - Type icon (colored badge: run=blue, lift=purple, wod=orange, bike=teal)
  - Title + meta line (duration, pace or weight context, avg HR for cardio)
  - Primary metric (e.g. 8.0 km, 55 min, 47.6 km)
  - TSS pill, color-coded by load: ≤50 grey, 51–80 amber, >80 red
  - Source pill (Strava / Manual)
  - Chevron indicating it's clickable
- Rows are clickable (full-row hit area) — clicking opens the detail panel (Issue 2)

## Data model
- Reads from existing `workouts` table — no schema changes for this ticket
- Week summary aggregates computed at query time (server-side, single endpoint)

## New endpoint
`GET /training_log?from=&to=&types=&search=`

Response shape (indented JSON sample):

    {
      "weeks": [
        {
          "week_start": "2026-05-26",
          "week_end": "2026-06-01",
          "label": "This week",
          "summary": {
            "workout_count": 2,
            "total_distance_km": 8.0,
            "total_tss": 113,
            "total_time_minutes": 93
          },
          "workouts": [
            {
              "id": "...",
              "date": "2026-05-27",
              "type": "run",
              "title": "Tempo run - Lumpini loops",
              "distance_km": 8.0,
              "duration_minutes": 38.7,
              "avg_hr": 162,
              "tss": 71,
              "source": "strava"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/log` route renders the page shell, week strip, filter bar, and workout list
- [ ] Week strip shows the current week by default; nav works
- [ ] Clicking a day pill scrolls to that day in the list (smooth scroll)
- [ ] Today is visually highlighted in the week strip
- [ ] Filter chips and search work; URL reflects state
- [ ] Workouts are grouped by week; each week shows a summary header
- [ ] TSS pill changes color by load threshold (≤50, 51–80, >80)
- [ ] Mobile responsive (≥380px) — week strip horizontally scrollable, filters stack
- [ ] Export button downloads visible workouts as CSV (date, type, title, distance, duration, tss, avg_hr, source)
- [ ] Page handles empty state ("No workouts in this range — log one or sync Strava")
- [ ] Page handles loading state

## Out of scope (separate tickets)
- Detail side panel — Issue 2
- Rest day rows from `daily_metrics` — Issue 3

## Depends on
- Sprint 10: Strava ingest (so Strava-sourced rows exist)
- Existing `workouts` table

**Repo:** `zealchaiwut/perf-coach`

## Goal
The side panel that opens when a user clicks a workout row on the Training Log page. Shows everything we know about that one session, including an LLM-generated coach note.

## Reference mockup
See `/mnt/user-data/outputs/perf-coach-training-log.html` — right column.

## Scope

**Layout**
- Slide-in or sticky side panel on desktop (~380px wide)
- Mobile: full-screen sheet with back button
- Header: workout title, date and time, source, close button
- Content sections (in order):
  1. 2×3 stat grid: Distance, Time, Avg pace (or weight context for strength), Avg HR, Elevation, TSS
  2. HR zone distribution — single horizontal stacked bar (Z1–Z5) with % labels for any zone ≥10%
  3. Splits — 1km bars for runs, 5km bars for rides, sets/reps/weight rows for strength
  4. Coach note — LLM-generated, purple card, 1–2 sentence interpretation
  5. User's notes — read-only block (edit mode in follow-up)
  6. Action buttons — "Open in Strava" (if applicable), "Edit"

**HR zones**
- Compute zones from the workout's HR stream (Strava) or skip section if no HR data
- Zone boundaries from user settings (Settings → HR zones); fall back to %max-HR defaults if not configured
- Reuse existing zone calculation if present; otherwise add a small helper

**Splits**
- For runs: 1km splits with pace and a bar (longer bar = slower split)
- Highlight the fastest split in green
- For strength: render sets-reps-weight-RPE per exercise instead of split bars

**Coach note (LLM)**
- New endpoint `POST /workouts/:id/coach_note` (cached server-side for 24h)
- Cache key is (workout_id, workout_updated_at) — invalidate if the workout is edited
- Fallback: hide section if LLM call fails (no error box)

Prompt skeleton (indented sample, not a code block):

    You are a concise endurance coach. Given this workout and the user's
    recent context, write 1-2 sentences interpreting the session. Reference
    specific numbers. Be direct. No fluff. Max 250 characters.

    WORKOUT:
    <json>

    RECENT CONTEXT (last 7 days):
    <summary>

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Clicking a workout row opens the detail panel with that workout's data
- [ ] Panel sticks to viewport on scroll (desktop)
- [ ] Mobile: full-screen sheet with working back/close
- [ ] Stat grid populates from workout fields; missing fields show "—"
- [ ] HR zones render when HR data exists; section hidden when not
- [ ] Splits render for runs (1km) and strength (per-exercise); other types show duration breakdown or hide
- [ ] Coach note generated once and cached; second open is instant
- [ ] Coach note references actual numbers from the workout (manual QA: pick known workout, confirm LLM cites correct distance/pace)
- [ ] LLM failure hides the section gracefully
- [ ] "Open in Strava" only shown for Strava-sourced workouts
- [ ] Edit button opens existing edit flow

## Out of scope
- Edit-in-place (use existing edit flow)
- Map preview (use "Open in Strava")
- Multi-turn coach Q&A (separate feature)
- Comparing two workouts side-by-side (later)

## Depends on
- Issue 1 (the list)
- LLM proxy from Sprint 11 (so we have a clean way to call the LLM)

**Repo:** `zealchaiwut/perf-coach`

## Goal
The Training Log lies if it only shows workout days. Rest days are signal too — they're when recovery happens. Show explicit lightweight rows for days that had a `daily_metrics` entry but no `workouts` row.

## Why it matters
Without this, the log looks sparse and the user can't see patterns like "I keep missing Wednesdays" or "Tuesday rest day = good Wednesday tempo." Rest days complete the story.

## Scope
- For each day in the selected range, check whether a workout exists. If not, but a `daily_metrics` row exists, render a rest-day row:
  - Date column (same shape as workout rows)
  - Label: "Rest day — sleep 6.8h, energy 3, mood 4"
  - Italic, muted styling (see mockup)
  - Not clickable for v1 (no detail panel)
- Days with no workout AND no daily metric → omit entirely (don't pad with empty rows)
- Rest days count toward the week summary only by displaying them; do not include in workout_count, distance, or TSS totals

## Endpoint change
- Extend `GET /training_log` response to include `rest_days` per week, OR interleave rest days into the same `workouts` array with a `type: "rest"` discriminator (pick one; latter is simpler client-side)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Days with daily_metrics but no workouts appear as rest-day rows in the list
- [ ] Rest rows are visually distinct (italic, muted) and not clickable
- [ ] Days with neither workout nor daily_metrics do NOT appear
- [ ] Week summary numbers unchanged (rest days don't pollute totals)
- [ ] Rest-day metadata pulled from `daily_metrics` (sleep, energy, mood) — show the most informative two or three values

## Out of scope
- Tapping a rest day to open a detail panel
- Editing daily metrics from the rest row
- "Why did I rest?" notes field — daily_metrics already has notes; not surfaced here

## Depends on
- Issue 1 (the list shell)
- Sprint 7: `daily_metrics` table
